wave: SECURITY / CENSUS BLINDNESS -- backend_roots was validated and documented but never actually consumed by either the filesystem walk or the external-provider capability grant
wave_title: A second delegated fresh-census investigation, scoped away from every area already covered this session, found that `RepoManifest.backend_roots` -- parsed from `.atlas/repo.toml`, validated for path-escape by `core::constraint::validate_manifest`, and explicitly documented in `.atlas/contracts/EXTERNAL-PROVIDER-TRUST.md#capability-minimum` as one of four fields 'joined against the repository root before walking the filesystem' -- was never actually joined anywhere. Both real consumers (`adapter::inventory_declared_source`, the filesystem-walk sink, and `runtime::prepare_work`'s `WorkRequest.allowed_paths` construction) only ever unioned `source_roots`/`frontend_roots`/`test_roots`, omitting `backend_roots` entirely.
priority_classification: security (priority 2) / census blindness (priority 4) -- `allowed_paths` is the literal capability-scoping data an external provider reads to know what it may touch; a legitimate, schema-supported, validated `backend_roots` entry not already covered by another field was invisible to census AND granted zero provider capability, silently contradicting this repository's own documented contract.
gap_discovered_by: A second delegated Explore-agent investigation, explicitly instructed to avoid every area already covered this session (the R4 Rust extractor, panic isolation, ADL recursion-DoS, CFG sweep, engineering_graph, and the two Cargo.toml fixes from the immediately preceding generation). It read `core::constraint::validate_manifest` (validates all four root fields), then `adapter::source::mod.rs::inventory_declared_source` and `runtime::lib.rs`'s `prepare_work` (both only union three of the four), and cross-checked against `.atlas/contracts/EXTERNAL-PROVIDER-TRUST.md`'s own explicit text naming all four fields as joined -- a direct contract-vs-implementation mismatch, not a speculative concern.
verification_before_acting: Re-read both consumer sites directly myself: `adapter/src/source/mod.rs`'s `inventory_declared_source` (only `source_roots`+`frontend_roots`+`test_roots`) and `runtime/src/lib.rs`'s `prepare_work` `allowed_paths` construction (the identical three-field omission) -- confirmed independently, not trusted from the subagent's line numbers alone.

Read `.atlas/contracts/EXTERNAL-PROVIDER-TRUST.md` line 206 directly: it explicitly names all four fields (`source_roots`/`backend_roots`/`frontend_roots`/`test_roots`) as joined against the repository root before walking the filesystem -- confirming this is a real contract violation, not merely a stylistic inconsistency.

Grepped the whole workspace for every reference to `backend_roots`: confirmed it is parsed from the manifest (`adapter::lib.rs`'s `array!("code", "backend_roots")`), validated (`core::constraint::validate_manifest`), and part of the typed schema (`core::schema::RepoManifest`) -- but literally never read anywhere else, confirming this is a genuine 'declared but never consumed' field, the same defect class as the `EngineeringGraph.evidence` bug fixed earlier this session.

Confirmed why this went unnoticed: this repository's own `.atlas/repo.toml` declares `backend_roots = ["core", "runtime", "adapter"]`, identical to its own `source_roots` -- so the omission was always masked by an exact duplicate in this repository's own self-census, never exercised by a distinct root.

Falsified both fixes independently: temporarily removed the `backend_roots` line from each of the two consumer sites in turn, re-ran the corresponding new test, confirmed it failed with the exact expected diagnostic, then restored the fix and re-ran to confirm it passes.

design_decisions.question: Fix the two inline call sites directly, or first extract `prepare_work`'s inline `allowed_paths` construction into its own pure function?
design_decisions.decision: Extracted a new `work_allowed_paths(manifest: Option<&RepoManifest>) -> Vec<String>` function in `runtime/src/lib.rs`, matching this file's own existing `resolve_dependency_closure`/`build_coverage_from_dependency_closure` precedent. Investigation confirmed `prepare_work`'s `allowed_paths` logic had NO direct unit test anywhere in the workspace before this fix -- it was only ever exercised indirectly through a full `systemize` pipeline run against a real on-disk repository, which is exactly why this specific omission went unnoticed for as long as it did (masked, on Atlas's own self-census, by the duplicate-roots coincidence). Extracting it into a small, directly testable function closes both the defect and the underlying testability gap that let it hide.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: Every root a `.atlas/repo.toml` manifest declares across all four fields (`source_roots`, `backend_roots`, `frontend_roots`, `test_roots`) is now walked by `inventory_declared_source` and granted as external-provider capability by `WorkRequest.allowed_paths`, matching `.atlas/contracts/EXTERNAL-PROVIDER-TRUST.md`'s own documented rule exactly. An ordinary manifest whose `backend_roots` duplicates another field (this repository's own shape) is completely unaffected, since both consumers already deduplicate.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: Two new tests in `adapter/src/source/mod.rs` (`a_backend_roots_only_entry_is_walked_not_silently_dropped`) and four new tests in `runtime/src/lib.rs` (`work_allowed_paths_includes_backend_roots_not_covered_by_any_other_field`, `work_allowed_paths_unions_all_four_fields_deduplicated_and_sorted`, `work_allowed_paths_filters_an_escaping_backend_root`, `work_allowed_paths_with_no_manifest_is_empty`). The two tests that actually exercise a non-overlapping `backend_roots` entry were each independently confirmed to fail without their corresponding fix (temporarily disabled, re-ran, restored) -- the other tests (dedup-when-overlapping, escaping-path filter, no-manifest case) were confirmed to still pass even without the fix, honestly demonstrating why the bug went unnoticed on this repository's own overlapping-roots shape rather than overstating test coverage.
stable_validator_law_compliance.independent_evidence_channel: cargo build --workspace clean. cargo fmt --all --check clean. cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean, zero warnings. Full cargo test --workspace: 285 adapter (+1), 2 apps/cli, 161 core, 72 runtime (+4) -- 520 total, 0 failed. `cargo run -q -p atlas-cli -- work prepare --root . --goal test` against this repository's own real manifest: allowed_paths unchanged (['adapter','adapter/tests','apps/studio','apps/studio/src','core','core/tests','runtime','runtime/tests']), confirming zero regression on Atlas's own self-census. `docs audit`: gate_ready true.

implementation.adapter_change: adapter/src/source/mod.rs -- `inventory_declared_source` now also unions `manifest.backend_roots`; the surrounding doc comments (on `declared_root_is_contained` and a new one on `inventory_declared_source` itself) now name all four fields, not three.
implementation.runtime_change: runtime/src/lib.rs -- extracted `work_allowed_paths(manifest: Option<&RepoManifest>) -> Vec<String>` (now including `backend_roots`) out of `prepare_work`'s previously-inline construction; `RepoManifest` newly imported.

adversarial_and_falsification_coverage: confirmed, by direct experiment, that the `work_allowed_paths_unions_all_four_fields_deduplicated_and_sorted` and `work_allowed_paths_filters_an_escaping_backend_root` tests would NOT have caught this regression on their own (both still pass with the fix removed, since their `backend_roots` values happen to overlap or be empty) -- only the dedicated non-overlapping-entry test does, which is exactly the shape that let this bug hide in Atlas's own self-census for as long as it did

grepped the entire workspace for every reference to `backend_roots` before concluding the fix's own scope was complete -- confirmed exactly two consumer sites needed the fix, no third silent copy of the same three-field union pattern exists elsewhere
verified end-to-end against this repository's own real manifest via the actual CLI (`work prepare`), not only the new unit tests in isolation

cargo test --workspace.totals: 285 adapter (+1), 2 apps/cli, 161 core, 72 runtime (+4) -- 520 total, 0 failed

cargo run -q -p atlas-cli -- work prepar.result: allowed_paths unchanged for this repository's own real manifest (backend_roots duplicates source_roots here)

recensus_scope_after_promotion: no prior CLOSED/EXTINCT conclusion is affected

a prior evidence record (`work-prepare-allowed-paths-defense-in-depth.json`) addressed a related but distinct concern (filtering escaping paths out of allowed_paths) in the same function -- that fix remains correct and is preserved verbatim inside the newly extracted `work_allowed_paths`; this generation does not revise that record's own claim, which was scoped to escape-filtering, not field completeness

the general lesson (a field parsed and validated by one layer but never actually read by any consumer is a real, recurring defect class in this codebase -- the same shape as the earlier EngineeringGraph.evidence bug) is worth keeping in mind for any future manifest schema field added without an accompanying consumer-side test

core::census::dependency.rs, adapter::source::frontend.rs (language detection), and the remainder of runtime::census::mod.rs::build_census were investigated this generation's own delegated pass and found already well-hardened -- not re-examined here
overall_verdict: MATERIALIZED AND VERIFIED. `backend_roots` -- declared, parsed, and validated since the field existed, and explicitly documented as joined into the filesystem walk -- is now actually consumed by both real consumers (`inventory_declared_source`, `WorkRequest.allowed_paths`). The `allowed_paths` construction was additionally extracted into a directly unit-testable pure function, closing the underlying testability gap that let this specific omission go unnoticed. Confirmed unaffected on this repository's own real manifest (backend_roots duplicates source_roots here), and confirmed via direct falsification that the fix's own dedicated regression test -- not the pre-existing dedup/escape-filter tests -- is what actually catches this defect. Full workspace suite (520 tests) passing, gate_ready true.
